text:
lina: heads-up: morning SAST batch shows a spike — ~140 new hits for repo service-core. lots are unverified because evidence attachments are missing.
omar: any infra changes overnight? we had an RBAC cleanup PR touch service accounts last night.
jo: I removed a couple project-level bindings as part of the tidy. I thought they were unused.
bot-scan: nightly-scan v4.0.0 complete. total findings: 140 (+110). missing evidence on PRs: [6012,6015]. upload errors: KMS_DECRYPT_ERROR x2; KMS_UNAUTHENTICATED x1.
pat: can you paste a runner log for the decrypt error?
lina: snippet from uploader logs:
```
2026-05-12T04:02:21Z ERROR evidence_uploader: decrypt failed: rpc error: code=PermissionDenied desc="cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt permission denied"
uploader: skipping attachment
```
jo: that matches my RBAC changes — I removed roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter at project level for sa-ci-runner.
omar: ok root cause likely RBAC removal. quick question: do we temporarily re-add project role or add a key-scoped binding?
pat: always prefer key-scoped. short-term restore scoped to the impacted crypto key is safest. example TF: 
```
resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding" "ci_uploader" {
  crypto_key_id = "projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/evidence/cryptoKeys/upload-key"
  role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
  members       = ["serviceAccount:sa-ci-runner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
}
```
jo: I'll open a small revert PR to restore key-level access and link it here.
bot-scan: audit note: KMS DataAccess logs include protoPayload.status.code=7 for the failed decrypt attempts against upload-key.
lina: why didn't our alerting catch the permission denies? current monitor only watches access counts, not DataAccess status codes.
omar: we should index protoPayload.status.code and map non-zero codes to evidence-upload alerts with the principal and key resource.
pat: also add a GH action preflight that impersonates the service account and tries a mock decrypt to validate permissions before merging RBAC changes. sample check: 
```
gcloud kms keys decrypt --location=global --keyring=evidence --key=upload-key \
  --ciphertext-file=/tmp/ct --plaintext-file=/tmp/pt \
  --impersonate-service-account=sa-ci-runner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
fail the check on non-zero exit.
jo: PR posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/714 — re-add key-scoped binding, small revert.
omar: approved, merging now. Also create an incident to track retro.
infra-bot: created INC-8199 "Evidence upload failures after RBAC tidy; KMS decrypt errors" assigned to eng-security.
lina: triggered an on-demand re-run of affected scans after merge.
bot-scan: manual-run nightly-2026-05-12-hotfix-1 started. evidence upload success increased; missing attachments resolved.
pat: next steps we should track: 1) add DataAccess -> scan-alert mapping in observability; 2) GH action preflight impersonation for any PRs touching scanner SA or KMS bindings; 3) infra PR template guidance for KMS principal formats and scoping; 4) update RBAC change playbook to call out CI/scanner dependencies.
jo: I'll own the infra template update and the revert PR. ETA: two small PRs by EOD.
omar: I'll own the observability changes — parse DataAccess.status.code and add an alert rule/Panel in Grafana.
lina: I'll write the blameless incident note in INC-8199 with timeline, impact, and owners. due date for follow-ups: 2026-05-19.
jo: sorry team, I misjudged the project-level cleanup. learned: assume scanners and CI likely depend on project-level bindings unless verified.
pat: no blame — good catch and quick recovery. add a single-line checklist to RBAC PRs: "Run SA impersonation preflight for pipelines that produce artifacts."
bot-scan: reaction :thumbsup: from 5 users.
